{"id": 197, "title": "legalbench-rule-application pack — Client letter: Halcyon Provisions commercial contract portfolio (Article 2 scoping)", "doc_type": "client_letter", "related_shape": "legalbench-rule-application", "body": "HALCYON PROVISIONS COMPANY

To the Commercial Group, Whitlock & Deene LLP:

args.rationale: Applying Whitlock & Deene's UCC Article 2 scope memo to Contract 3 (Marovic Equipment bottling line agreement): total contract price = $290,000; goods component (MX-9 bottling line machinery) = $248,000; services component (on-site installation, calibration, operator training) = $42,000. Predominant purpose test arithmetic: half of $290,000 = $145,000; goods component of $248,000 exceeds half ($248,000 > $145,000), and the goods component exceeds the services component ($248,000 > $42,000), so MORE THAN HALF of the total contract price is attributable to goods. Under the memo's hybrid-contract rule, when more than half of the price is attributable to goods the ENTIRE contract is governed by UCC Article 2 (no split). Therefore UCC Article 2 governs the entire Contract 3 — disposition: approved.
